same source, classic fixups -- the varargs ABI is a libSystem property, not a fixup one
mach_task_self, vm_allocate/protect/deallocate, mach_absolute_time, timebase, mach_error_string
errno numbering, O_* flag values and struct stat layout all differ between Darwin and Linux
a representative hand-built utility: ctype (a DATA table Darwin inlines into the guest), setlocale, getopt, qsort, strftime, fgets
every loaded image sits below 2^47, because libswiftCore has the 47-bit isa mask compiled in
struct dirent is 1048 bytes on Darwin and 280 on glibc, with d_type and d_name at different offsets; readdir translates rather than forwards
condition variables that really block, and the RECURSIVE/ERRORCHECK constants Darwin and glibc swap
all 128 _SC_* names differ between Darwin and glibc, so sysconf must translate rather than forward
struct passwd is 72 bytes on Darwin and 48 on glibc; pw_dir falls off the end of a forwarded one
std::sort really sorts all five hand-instantiated types; the broken version recursed forever
sigset_t is 4 bytes on Darwin and 128 on glibc, ten signal numbers differ, and SIG_BLOCK/UNBLOCK/SETMASK are off by one
Apple's typed allocator; the size argument sits in a different register in every member of the family
walks a real stack through Apple's compact __unwind_info; the symbols resolved the whole time it was stubbed
poll(2) across the boundary: the eight agreeing flags, the counts, and the wrapper's heap path -- a regression guard, since the two flags that differ cannot be reached from a fixture
installing a handler: struct sigaction is 16 bytes against 152, not one sa_flags bit agrees, and the signal NUMBER has to be translated again on the way back INTO guest code
a real C++ throw across frames, caught by type; the case that matters is the handler that must NOT match
fcntl's command agrees and its O_* value does not; madvise's four common advice values agree and MADV_FREE, the only one libdispatch uses, does not
PTHREAD_CREATE_JOINABLE is 1 here and DETACHED there, so the safe-looking direction is the broken one; SCHED_OTHER is glibc's SCHED_FIFO
loading a dylib at RUN TIME: the export trie through a handle, the initialiser, the TLV, and a bind from the new image into an old one
the five MIBs CF needs; KERN_PROC_PID gates __CFInitialize and returns a 648-byte BSD struct CF reads one field from
which image and symbol an address is in, plus RTLD_NEXT/SELF/MAIN_ONLY -- one gap, not three: all of them needed THE CALLING IMAGE
_NSGetExecutablePath must name the GUEST, not the loader -- /proc/self/exe is a real path and the wrong one; plus pthread_atfork, which glibc has no dynamic symbol for
the _dyld_* image table: index 0 is the main executable, and the slide must agree with __TEXT's vmaddr -- only the loader can answer any of it
OSAtomic returns the NEW value, not the old -- add_fetch against fetch_add, off by exactly one operation; plus OSSpinLock excluding under eight threads
RLIMIT_NOFILE is 8 here and 7 there, and Darwin's 8 is Linux's MEMLOCK -- a forward returns a memory limit as a descriptor count; plus PTHREAD_SCOPE off by one
@loader_path in a dlopen means the CALLER's directory, so two images in two directories asking for the same string must get two different files
the environment was two arrays with one name -- environ from the loader's envp, getenv from glibc's -- agreeing until the first write
__exp10 COMPUTES rather than branching to itself -- the catalogued idiom bug -- plus flsl, which glibc has only as ffsl, one letter and a whole word apart
readdir_r returns an ERRNO and signals EOF through result, not -1 -- a wrapper returning -1 makes every caller's loop terminate as an error
variadic, so it cannot be forwarded -- every argument is a pointer glibc would write through; the length modifier decides the WIDTH OF THE STORE

Mach's in-task virtual copy: no alignment requirement at all, MEMMOVE semantics on overlap (the checksum separates that from a forward copy by 16), and unmapped/PROT_NONE/read-only all give KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS rather than KERN_PROTECTION_FAILURE

struct utsname is 1280 bytes with 256-byte fields on Darwin and 390 with 65-byte ones in glibc, so a forward is safe on SIZE and wrong on every OFFSET; plus the sentinel check for Darwin writing strlen+1 bytes and leaving the rest of the field alone

struct group is 32 bytes with the SAME offsets on both sides -- so unlike passwd there is no layout to translate, and what is left is the pthread-style errno RETURN (ERANGE is 34 on both, which is what lets an untranslated one pass) plus the not-found contract, rc 0 with *result NULL

the option flags ROTATE (Darwin XATTR_CREATE 0x02 IS Linux XATTR_REPLACE 0x02, so create-if-absent performs replace-if-present), XATTR_NOFOLLOW is a flag here and a different FUNCTION there, the arity differs over Darwin's resource-fork position, and Linux refuses every name outside user./security./system./trusted.

the argument ORDER is swapped (Darwin path,cmd against Linux cmd,special) and the first argument is a mount point against a block device -- but APFS supports no quotas at all, so ENOTSUP is what Darwin itself answers and this grades that byte for byte

FTSENT is 112 bytes on Darwin and 120 on glibc; translated traversal grades children/set, NOSTAT/NAMEONLY safety, Darwin-only COMFOLLOWDIR/NOSTAT_TYPE, pre-read roots, nested comparators, root-parent and symlink-follow state, guest persistence, and fresh generations after exact-address reuse

Darwin has THREE public static mutex initialisers and the SIGNATURE WORD IS THE TYPE -- a constant no call site names because the guest's compiler laid it down; CF's CFLockInit is the ERRORCHECK one, and adopting it as a default would lock and unlock perfectly while dropping the checking, so this grades semantics by RETURN VALUE

snprintf_l must route through OUR formatter because Darwin's varargs are on the STACK and AAPCS64's are in registers, and its locale_t is enforced by construction (libSystem exports setlocale and nothing else, so a guest cannot build one); pthread_threadid_np is graded for a real id by the cross-thread line

the dedupe contract, and it is an ASYMMETRY: a SYMLINK to a loaded dylib is ONE image, two DISTINCT files sharing an install name are TWO -- a loader deduping on install name fails the second half in the direction that looks like an improvement
